feeds.title: Exceptional Individuals
feeds.description: As a social enterprise, we support and help neurodivergent people find work, in order to give back to society. Check out our latest posts on all things neurodiversity.

feeds.title: Different Brains Blog
feeds.description: Different Brains strives to encourage understanding & acceptance of individuals who have variations in brain function and social behaviors known as neurodiversity. Our mission has 3 pillars:To mentor neurodiverse adults in maximizing their potential for employment and independence, to increase awareness of neurodiversity by producing interactive media and to foster the next generation of neurodivergent self-advocates.

feeds.title: Neurodivergent Rebel
feeds.description: The Neurodivergent Rebel opened their blog in 2016 as a way to introduce people unfamiliar with the concept of neurodiversity to this new way of seeing the neurological differences. The blog explores the ideology of neurodiversity and the creative expressions of autistic people.

feeds.title: Adjust Blog
feeds.description: Our aim is to start the Neurodiversity conversation in every workplace. Neurodiversity is the concept that we recognise, value and celebrate that we all think differently. Adjust provides employers with a clear, practical and positive understanding of Neurodiversity. We focus on four neurotypes including autism, dyslexia, dyspraxia and ADHD.

feeds.title: Reflections
feeds.description: Kristy Forbes is a leading autistic adult & support specialist for autistic people, their families & professionals; & the Founding Director of inTune Pathways. Here you will find written blog pieces on neurodivergence, the language and behaviours of autism, ADHD, pathological demand avoidance (PDA), and other neurodivergent, lived experiences, by Kristy Forbes.

feeds.title: Autistic Women & Nonbinary Network (AWN) Blog
feeds.description: The mission of Autistic Women & Nonbinary Network (AWN) is to provide community, support, and resources for Autistic women, girls, transfeminine and transmasculine nonbinary people, trans people of all genders, Two-Spirit people, and all others of marginalized genders.AWN Network is dedicated to building a supportive community where we can share our experiences in an understanding, diverse and inclusive environment.

feeds.title: NeuroDiversity 2.0
feeds.description: Judy Singer is an Australian sociologist. She is recognized as being instrumental in the development of a the concept of Neurodiversity while an compete and Honours Degree at the University of Technology Sydney (UTS) in 1997-8.

feeds.title: Critical Neurodiversity
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Robert Chapman. I'm a neurodivergent academic with an interest in emancipatory politics, social theory, disability, and mental health. I began this blog in 2016 as a place to explore and develop critical neurodiversity theory and related issues.

feeds.title: Open Doors Therapy Blog
feeds.description: Open Doors Therapy's autism experts offer individual & group therapy for neurodiverse adults, teens & caregivers. Here you will find articles about neurodiversity in adults and teens. Topics include social skills in the workplace, women with autism, and navigating college on the spectrum.

feeds.title: Aviva Seigler
feeds.description: Aviva Seigler is the executive director at Autistic Inclusive Meets the USA and a website editor for Autistic Inclusive Meets. She is a writer, an activist, and an advocate. Her hope is to bridge the gap between allies and autistics while fighting the pseudoscience that threatens all people, not just autistics.

feeds.title: Ayoa » Neurodiversity
feeds.description: Ayoa is an all-in-one online whiteboard where you can brainstorm ideas, work together and get things done. Read our informative articles related to neurodiversity.

feeds.title: Neuro Clastic
feeds.description: Content about autism by autistic and neurodivergent people. Neuro Clastic is a collective of actually autistic writers and artists advocating for autistic representation and human rights.

feeds.title: Me.Decoded
feeds.description: Founded by Helen Needham, Me.Decoded is dedicated to the promotion of Neurodiversity - by bringing together the Neurodivergent and allies who are committed to embracing Neurodiversity.

feeds.title: Diversity and Ability
feeds.description: D&A is a disabled-led social enterprise supporting students, organizations, and social justice projects to create inclusive cultures. Our disabled-led team shares their top tips, lived experiences, and favourite resources on diversity and inclusion and disability justice.

feeds.title: The Musical Autist Blog
feeds.description: Our mission is to provide equal rights to the fine arts and to create platforms for self advocacy, by giving credentialed music therapists the tools and resources they need to facilitate Sensory Friendly Concerts in their own local communities.

feeds.title: Neurodiverse Self Advocacy Blog
feeds.description: The Neurodiverse Self Advocacy (NDSA) is a space where neurodivergent people support each other and advocate as a group. Led by autistic volunteers, our mission is to transform attitudes to autism and develop new services relevant to us all.

feeds.title: Lexxic | News & Blog
feeds.description: Lexxic was established in 2007 by Chartered Occupational Psychologist Nicola James, after managing the challenges of her own dyslexia in the corporate sector. We post new articles each month on neurodiversity in the workplace.

feeds.title: In the Loop About Neurodiversity
feeds.description: Welcome, and thank you for stopping by! My name is Cassandra Crosman, and I am the creator of 'In the Loop About Neurodiversity.' I am a 23 year old neurodivergent college student who has studied various subjects in humanities and social science such as communication studies, philosophy, and political science. In the Loop About Neurodiversity is a platform that seeks to educate others on what neurodiversity is and how to better serve neurodiverse people.

feeds.title: Spectrum Women
feeds.description: The Spectrum Women mentors provide one on one services for neurodivergent adults to help them in working towards a future that is fulfilling and determined by their visions and goals.

feeds.title: NeuroEmploy
feeds.description: We at NeuroEmploy aim to change the narrative, find innovative and productive ways to support neurodivergent people into and at work, and educate employers and businesses on the value of having neurodiversity in the workplace.

feeds.title: Sapien Labs » Neurodiversity
feeds.description: Sapien Labs is a not for profit organization founded in 2016 with a mission to understand and enable the human mind.

feeds.title: Coaching focused on Strengths and Neurodiversity
feeds.description: Brilliantly Diverse offers education and coaching services for anyone who wants to shine in life, live their values, and attain their goals and feels their 'difference' may be getting in the way of achievement. We help you uncover your strengths!

feeds.title: Neurodiversity News Blog
feeds.description: My main aim is to inform those who support neurodiversity with the latest news regarding the movement. That news will also be aided with weekly interviews by various neurodiversity activists and allies. I hope to make the world a better place for disabled people the way I know best: by keeping audiences informed.
